clue.text: Making a pile's discerning!

indicators.note: making something new out of these letters means they are rearranged into a fresh order

parts.note: the possessive is read as a plain plural here, piles

explanation.surface: An exclamation that building up a heap shows real discernment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' signals an anagram of A PILES; the apostrophe is ignored, so pile's supplies its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is the act of spying or catching sight of something, a noticing or perceiving.

clue.text: Captivating the listener in the finale

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for the finale

parts.note: a finale is an ending
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Praise for a gripping closing section of a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EAR inside ENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something charming that wins affection; synonyms.

clue.text: .Stops to stretch and have a drink

parts.note: to pull a muscle or rope is to stretch it
to sup is to sip or drink

explanation.surface: Someone halts their walk to do a few stretches and take a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray dot before 'Stops' is a printing mark, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or rider that pulls up comes to a halt; a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Seat driver badly and, he will give notice

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A chauffeur who seats someone clumsily is told he is going to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give notice' suggests resigning or firing; here it means announcing goods in public.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertiser makes products known through public announcements, giving notice of them.

clue.text: Lawyers, over a period, created peers

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
on can mean over, as in a lid on a jar
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Lawyers who over time were ennobled.
explanation.definitionFit: The baronage is the body of barons, nobles whose rank is conferred by the Crown.

clue.text: "Beware the pine-tree's withered branch! Beware the ' awful (Longfellow)

definitions.text: "Beware the pine-tree's withered branch! Beware the ' awful (Longfellow)

parts.words: "Beware the pine-tree's withered branch! Beware the ' awful (Longfellow)
parts.note: a quotation from Longfellow's poem Excelsior with the final word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A line from Longfellow's poem Excelsior, warning a climber of mountain dangers, with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a blank after 'awful'; the missing word completes the line, a warning of snow sliding down the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem warns of a mass of snow and ice crashing down an Alpine slope, which is the missing threat.

clue.text: A player holds none in honour

indicators.note: in places the word for none inside the abbreviation for the honour

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
O is the figure nought, meaning none

explanation.surface: A sportsman who has received no award from the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a sportsman; here it is a musical instrument that is played.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, something that is played in an orchestra.

clue.text: Trouble a barrier is required to contain it

indicators.note: to contain means the barrier word wraps round the following piece

parts.note: a gate is a barrier across a gap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fence is needed to keep something in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts IT inside GATE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to disturb or upset them; a verb synonym.

clue.text: The student's let-out

parts.note: a permission slip letting a pupil or college member leave the premises for a while

explanation.definitionFit: An exeat, Latin for 'let him go out', is leave of absence granted to a boarder or undergraduate.

clue.text: There are other ranks --. a number, it's said

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, the non-officers
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A remark about the private soldiers and how many there are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' looks like a homophone signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral statement is a spoken one, not written down.

clue.text: A. Digger will accommodate one free

indicators.note: will accommodate means the digger word houses another piece within it

parts.note: a delver is one who digs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An excavator who will put someone up without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will accommodate' puts I inside DELVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver is to set free or rescue, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: How to make a spray is in a book

indicators.note: in puts the short word inside the word for a large book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for producing an aerosol are printed in a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IS inside TOME, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomise a liquid is to break it into fine droplets, the way a spray works.

clue.text: Antipodean saturnalia — should -be broken up

indicators.note: broken up means the letters of the festival's name are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A demand that a wild Roman-style festival be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: Saturnalia was the Roman winter festival; its letters rearrange into the answer. The stray hyphen before 'be' is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia lies at the Antipodes from Britain, so its people are antipodeans.

clue.text: Unable to move at speed

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck while trying to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: one sense is fixed firmly in place, the other is quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck firm, as a ship held immobile, and quick, as a runner moving rapidly: two senses of one word.

clue.text: Have no man washing outside in this part of London

indicators.note: outside says the word for washing wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a bath is a wash
to lack is to have none
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A complaint that no man in this London district takes a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts BATH around LACK + HE. Blackheath is a district and common in south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackheath is a district of south-east London known for its open heath.

clue.text: Suggested a mischievous child -wasn't telling the truth

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lied means told an untruth

explanation.surface: An accusation that a naughty child was being dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray hyphen before 'wasn't' is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest without stating; past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Let off as a result of underworld instruction

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm
a charge is an instruction, as a judge's charge to a jury

explanation.surface: A gangster fires a weapon on the orders of the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests gangsters; here it is the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a gun is to fire it, or a prisoner to release him; both are letting off.

clue.text: Gather together for a little prayer

explanation.surface: An invitation to assemble for a short act of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or assemble; and a short liturgical prayer, stressed on the first syllable, said in church services.

clue.text: Youngsters eat greens only if properly prepared

indicators.note: properly prepared means the letters are made up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Advice that young people will only eat their vegetables if well cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly prepared' signals an anagram of EAT GREENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are young people aged from thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Revered figure having to trail back, lacking the right clothing

indicators.note: back says the word for trail is turned round end to end

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail or follow them

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for right is missing from the clothing word

parts.note: dress is clothing
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A venerated person forced to follow behind without proper clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DOG into GOD; 'lacking' removes R from DRESS to leave DESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A goddess is a female deity, an object of worship.

clue.text: Boy holds pets up to make a point

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
holds means the boy word has the pets word inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
mice are kept as pets

explanation.surface: A boy holds his pets up to show something.
explanation.walkthrough: LAD holding MICE gives LAMICED; 'up' reverses it all. The definition is 'to make a point', as a decimal point does.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal fraction is written with a point separating whole numbers from tenths.

clue.text: One who got away with directions to head East

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: A fugitive given instructions to make for the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a noun, a headland, not the verb to make for.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is someone who has escaped, such as a prisoner on the run.

clue.text: Directed a great deal in black and white

indicators.note: in puts the word for a great deal inside the word for black and white

parts.note: pied means of two colours, especially black and white
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: A film shot largely in monochrome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directed' suggests a film director; here it means steered.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to steer or guide a course; past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Formerly part of the coronation ceremony

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something used to be included in the crowning ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at some time in the past; adverb synonyms.

clue.text: It's not usual not in a branch of the army

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A remark that it is odd for someone to be absent from a military corps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link word. RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional or bizarre, beyond the bounds of the ordinary.

clue.text: Feature about a mount-a creature with a lovely coat

definitions.text: a creature with a lovely coat

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
c is short for circa, about
a mount is a hill

explanation.surface: A face, a horse and an animal admired for its fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' suggests a horse; here it is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinchilla is a South American rodent prized for its soft dense fur.

clue.text: A bird sanctuary

parts.note: not a nature reserve but the safe home a single bird builds for its young

explanation.definitionFit: A nest is the shelter a bird builds, a refuge for its eggs and chicks.

clue.text: Turned into acid

explanation.surface: Something was converted into an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that has turned has gone off; acid describes a sharp, tart taste; both are senses of one word.

clue.text: A doctor has to travel around to find such an instrument

indicators.note: around says the travel word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: to tour is to travel round
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor must go on a journey to locate a particular instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts A + MB inside TOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambour is a drum, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Surprise beginning to French article

parts.note: a start is a beginning
le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: Unexpected start to a piece of writing in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a piece of writing; here it is a grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give a sudden shock or fright; verb synonyms.

clue.text: Increased by five hundred after general reorganisation

indicators.note: after places the numeral at the end of the rearranged letters
reorganisation means the letters of the word general are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Numbers swelled by five hundred after a commander reshuffled his staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganisation' rearranges GENERAL to make ENLARGE; D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make bigger, so enlarged means made greater in size.

clue.text: An island with sound ways

indicators.note: with sound says the word for ways is to be heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: roads are ways

explanation.surface: An island with healthy, well-made routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy; it tells us to listen. Rhodes is a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean, the largest of the Dodecanese.
